The Blues' attack was humming early. (Getty Images: Bradley Kanaris)

NSW have created history, winning a Lang Park State of Origin decider for just the fourth time in 14 attempts.

The Blues ran out to an 18-0 lead in front of a near-capacity crowd at Lang Park, and then produced a professional second half to seal Game III, and the series with a 30-12 victory.

Blues halfback Nathan Cleary was a star for his state, with two tries, a one-on-one strip that led to a try, and converting all five of his goal attempts.

"He was unbelievable, the ice man," Cleary's NSW and Penrith teammate Liam Martin told ABC Sport.

"He certainly silenced the critics. Just honoured to play alongside him."

Speaking to the Nine Network after the match, Cleary heaped praise on coach Laurie Daley, who had faced plenty of criticism during the campaign.

“A lot of people wrote him off and negative things were said about him, but he’s an absolute champion in NSW and we never write off champions,” Cleary said.

“I love the guy and I’m so pumped for him.”

The win is the Blues' third consecutive Origin win in Brisbane, with two of those being Game III deciders.

Relive all the action from Game III in the live blog below.

This is where we will end the live blog tonight.

The shield will be south of the Tweed River for a year.

Thank-you for joining us this evening.

ABC Sport will have a live blog of every NRL match as we now focus on the run to the finals.

Wed 8 Jul 2026 at 11:30pm

By Michael Doyle

— reporting by AAP

NSW have won the State of Origin series after Nathan Cleary starred in a stunning 30-12 upset win over Queensland in the decisive third game at Lang Park.

Winless in his first three Origin deciders, under-fire halfback Cleary helped the Blues to a surprise 18-0 lead by scoring two first-half tries and stripping the ball ahead of their third.

Game-ending head injuries to veteran fullback James Tedesco and first-gamer Jack Bostock weakened the Blues, who were troubled by the injection of Maroons livewire Reece Walsh in the second half.

Chasing points, the Maroons had a try chalked off that would have put them six points behind in the final 15 minutes, with the bunker ruling Max Plath had been offside chasing Sam Walker's kick.

Player-of-the-match Cleary then nailed a penalty goal that made it a three-score game, all but putting the result beyond doubt.

It marked only the Blues' fourth victory in a decider at Lang Park from 14 attempts, and their first time winning consecutive deciders at the venue following their 2024 triumph.

The victory came after the Blues were written off by all and sundry, having conceded 36 second-half points in a demoralising 20-point Game II loss.

With last year's series loss fresh in memory, coach Laurie Daley faced heavy scrutiny ahead of the decider.

No player had been under more pressure to deliver in Brisbane than Cleary, for so long criticised for his track record in big Origin moments.

The four-time premiership winner wasted little time silencing his doubters on Wednesday night.

After an error-prone start from the Maroons, Cleary had the Blues' first try stepping inside Kurt Capewell at close range and gliding over.

Blues second-rower Liam Martin, back from a knee injury, burst through Cameron Munster and found Stephen Crichton, who flicked to Mark Nawaqanitawase ahead of Cleary's second try.

In the Maroons' next set, Cleary stripped the ball from Selwyn Cobbo to put the Blues into position for another four-pointer through Cameron Murray.

The Blues lost Tedesco in the final minute before half-time when the former captain clashed heads with Maroons second-rower Briton Nikora.

Tolu Koula shifted to fullback, before the Blues were forced into another backline reshuffle when Jack Bostock fell awkwardly contesting a kick.

Walsh and Kalyn Ponga combined to give the Maroons a sniff, the pair helping Cobbo to a try and cutting the deficit to 10.

But just as the Maroons were on the attack again, Jojo Fifita fumbled Walsh's kick into the arms of Bradman Best, who ran 100 metres to score the Blues' fourth.

After Fifita atoned on the right, the Maroons thought they had a fourth try when Koula allowed a Walker kick to bounce up for Rob Toia.

But the offside penalty against Plath thwarted the Maroons and the Blues held on, with Hudson Young crossing late.

Wed 8 Jul 2026 at 11:26pm

By Michael Doyle

Queensland hooker Harry Grant has spoken to ABC Sport's John Gibbs following tonight's defeat in Game III.

You don't want to come out of these games on the losing side, but that was us tonight. NSW played a really good game. They were clinical throughout the 80 minutes; you've got to give them credit for the game they played.

Key Event

Wed 8 Jul 2026 at 11:17pm

By Michael Doyle

Laurie Daley has praised captain Isaah Yeo as "the best leader I've come across".

I understand now why Penrith have had so much success.

Yeo is the best leader I've come across.

He is very calm, very measured.

You can have a conversation with him, man-to-man.

When you have a good relationship with leaders, you can discuss things. He drives it all. He's empowered to do that.

Key Event

Wed 8 Jul 2026 at 11:16pm

By Michael Doyle

NSW coach Laurie Daley and captain Isaah Yeo are speaking to the media.

Here are his initial reactions.

Just so proud of the performance. That's the type of performance I thought was there.

We have moments in Game I and Game II, but we just weren't consistent.

That was a magnificent performance tonight, to come up here and do what we did.

I knew the best was yet to come.

Wed 8 Jul 2026 at 11:08pm

By Michael Doyle

Queensland coach Billy Slater and captain Cam Munster are speaking to the media.

Slater says he is disappointed with the result, but proud of the effort from his players.

We just weren't quite good enough tonight. Didn't quite get our best performance on the field.

We never gave up; we had our chances, but we hurt ourselves a few times.

Slater was asked about the length-of-the-field try to NSW centre Bradman Best.

The Bunker appeared to have a longer look at the replay before confirming the try, with at least one camera potentially showing a knock-on in the lead-up from NSW winger Jack Bostock.

Slater said he didn't get a good enough look at any replay to make a comment on the try being awarded.

We didn't get a clear look in the box. It is what it is.

Key Event

Wed 8 Jul 2026 at 10:45pm

By Michael Doyle

NSW Blues coach Laurie Daley has coached his State to a State of Origin decider win.

It is also the second series win Daley has coached.

Much has been made about Daley's track record coaching Origin matches, but he put many demons to bed, tonight.

He has just spoken to the Nine Network.

“It’s pretty special,” Daley said.

“I was just happy for the players. Obviously we know that performance was there, but we just haven’t seen it, so it was all about for us proving ourselves right.”

Wed 8 Jul 2026 at 10:40pm

By Michael Doyle

Wed 8 Jul 2026 at 10:30pm

By Michael Doyle

There was so much said and written about the State of Origin record for both NSW halfback Nathan Cleary, and coach Laurie Daley.

But that can be put to bed now with a magnificent victory tonight.

Speaking on the Nine Network, Cleary has praised the NSW coach after the pair, aliong with the rest of the squad, created made history tonight.

“A lot of people wrote him off and negative things were said about him, but he’s an absolute champion in NSW and we never write off champions,” Cleary said.

“I love the guy and I’m so pumped for him.”

Key Event

Wed 8 Jul 2026 at 10:22pm

By Michael Doyle

Wed 8 Jul 2026 at 10:22pm

By Michael Doyle

What a night for Bradman Best.

He comes back into the side, scores the decisive try to win the match, just like he did in 2024.

He is speaking to ABC Sport, and highlights that his year started with a few injuries.

To get the opportunity to come back, I had a few injuries to start the year. When this opportunity come up, I wanted to take it with both hands. We knew coming up here, it's always go to be a tough ask.

Speaking of his length-of-the-field try, Best downplayed how brilliant he was.

I was just lucky enough. The ball stood up for me there. I had a bit of work to do.

Wed 8 Jul 2026 at 10:19pm

By Michael Doyle

Cameron Murray came off the bench and was brilliant tonight.

He, along with the enitre NSW forward pack were excellent.

Here is his initial reaction with ABC Sport's John Gibbs.

It's hard to put into words. It's and awesome night. Theses are the ones you want to play in.

The NSW forwards did a great job at shutting down the Queensland halves through long periods of the contest.

Murray tells ABC Sport, stopping Queensland's playmakers was something the NSW forward took personally this week.

We spoke a lot about how dangerous their playmakers are. I think every forward stepped up in our team tonight.

Wed 8 Jul 2026 at 10:15pm

By Michael Doyle

Liam Martin was called in for Game III, and he produced the goods for NSW.

He is speaking to ABC Sport's John Gibbs.

"I think everyone did their job fantastically. We just killed it. Incredable."

NSW were on top for much of the game, but Queensland kept themselves in the contest with timely tries.

But it was the way the Blues were able to respond each time that was crucial tonight.

"I think we responded after points really well," Martin said.

Wed 8 Jul 2026 at 10:08pm

By Michael Doyle

It is an exclamation point.

NSW throw the ball around on the final play as the siren sounds.

A Blues player goes down with the ball and is not held.

The footy spills backwards, and Hudson Young is there to pick up the ball and score the try.

NSW has declined the conversion attempt.

Wed 8 Jul 2026 at 10:06pm

By Michael Doyle

NSW are still playing footy. They are savouring this moment.

A kick ahead is fielded near the in-goal by Maroons fullback Kalyn Ponga (who is back on).

NSW's Stephen Crichton drags the Queensland number one into the in-goal.

There is a huge NEW SOUTH WALES chant in Lang Park.

Key Event

Wed 8 Jul 2026 at 10:03pm

By Michael Doyle

The Maroons need five perfect minutes of footy, and three tries to win this game.

KNOCK-ON.

Queensland winger Selwyn Cobbo takes a great catch near his own goal-line, but then drops the ball in the tackle.

NSW have the ball. NSW is attacking the Queensland goal-line, and there is less than five minutes in the match.

That should all; lay-down misère.

The Blues are going to win the State of Origin series.

Key Event

Wed 8 Jul 2026 at 9:55pm

By Michael Doyle

From 38 metres out, 15 metres in from the right touchline, Nathan Cleary nails the penalty goal attempt.

That never looked like missing.

Cleary has had some great games in his career, and this is one of the best (in this blogger's view).

QLD 12

NSW 26

Wed 8 Jul 2026 at 9:54pm

By Michael Doyle

NSW has been given a penalty, about 38 metres from the Queensland goal-line.

Tolutau Koula took a run, and then Queensland's Hamiso Tabuai-Fidow lifted him between the legs and put the NSW back in a dangerous position.

No doubt, that is a penalty.

Nathan Cleary is going to attempt the kick at goal to give NSW a 14-point lead.
